meta.titre: School Life and the Education System: who runs schools and how
meta.sous_theme: Types of schools, school administration and school rules

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: On the first day of term, a Form 1 pupil asks why her cousin's school ends every morning with prayers while her own school does not. The reason lies in who owns and runs each school. The Cameroonian education system includes government schools, schools of churches and other religious bodies, private schools opened by individuals and technical schools, and each type has its own features. At the GCE, you are asked to recognise these types, to know who does what in a school, and to explain why rules and participation matter.

items: A school is an institution in which pupils learn under the guidance of teachers.
A rule is a statement that tells people what they may or may not do.
Education helps a person to acquire knowledge, skills and good behaviour.

sections.titre: How schools are owned, organised and ruled
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Types of schools by ownership
| Type | Owner and manager | Typical features |
|---|---|---|
| Public (government) school | The State | Teachers are recruited and paid by the State, and the school follows official rules |
| Denominational school | A church or another religious body | Moral and religious formation is stressed, while the national curriculum is followed and freedom of worship is respected |
| Private lay school | An individual, a family or a company | Run by the owner, who fixes fees within the law, and follows the official programme |

### Types by kind of training
General schools prepare pupils mainly for further study and the GCE or other certificates. Technical and vocational schools train pupils in practical skills, so they have workshops and laboratories whose tools and materials are kept and controlled by the school authorities under the principal. Cameroon has two sub-systems of education, the Anglophone and the Francophone, each with its own examinations.

### Who does what
- The **principal** leads the school and answers to the State authorities and, in a private or denominational school, to the owner.
- **Teachers** teach, assess and guide pupils.
- Staff in charge of discipline and guidance keep order and help pupils with problems.
- **Prefects and class monitors** assist teachers and set an example.
- The **Parent-Teacher Association (PTA)** brings parents and staff together to support the school, for example by helping to build classrooms or to buy equipment.

### Why the State is involved
The Constitution provides that the State guarantees the right of the child to education, that primary education is compulsory and that the State organises and supervises education at all levels.

### School rules
Rules cover attendance, punctuality, uniform, respect, care of property and honesty in exams. They protect the safety and the rights of everybody and create a good environment for learning.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a school is described and the type must be named
variantes.contenu_markdown: Find the owner first. A school owned by a religious body is denominational. A school owned by the State is public. A school opened by a person or a company is private lay. Then name one feature that confirms your answer.

variantes.nom: Questions on roles in a school
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks 'who' or 'role of'
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the person or body, then give the task in one sentence, then add the benefit for pupils. Example: the PTA supports the school by raising funds for infrastructure, which improves learning conditions.
Give four or five points, each with a reason: rules keep order, protect safety, teach responsibility and prepare pupils for life in the society.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the model answer to this question: (a) Name two types of school according to ownership. (b) Explain two ways in which the Parent-Teacher Association can help a school. [6 marks]

etapes.justification: 'Name' needs only the types. 'Explain' needs a developed answer for each way.
The question is about ownership, so the types must differ by owner.

etapes.action: List the roles of the PTA for (b).
etapes.justification: Choose roles that match what parents can actually do.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Raising funds for infrastructure and equipment; helping to settle problems between school and families.

etapes.justification: Add the reason that the role benefits pupils.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Funds give pupils classrooms and benches; dialogue between parents and staff improves discipline and attendance.

etapes.justification: Two types and two roles were asked for.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
(a) Two types of school according to ownership are the **public (government) school**, owned by the State, and the **denominational school**, owned by a church or another religious body.

(b) First, the PTA can raise money from parents to build or repair classrooms and to buy equipment, so that pupils study in better conditions. Second, the PTA creates a link between parents and the school administration, so that problems of discipline, absence or fees are discussed and settled together, which helps pupils to progress.

items.erreur_markdown: A student states that all schools in Cameroon are owned by the Government.
items.pourquoi_faux: Many schools belong to religious bodies, to individuals or to companies.
items.correction_markdown: Name the owner: State (public), religious body (denominational), individual or company (private lay).

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes that 'the PTA is a group of pupils who help the teachers'.
items.pourquoi_faux: The PTA is made of parents and teachers, not of pupils.
items.correction_markdown: The Parent-Teacher Association brings together parents and school staff to support the school.

items.erreur_markdown: A student says that a denominational school may refuse to teach the official programme.
items.pourquoi_faux: These schools follow the national curriculum and prepare pupils for the official examinations, while adding religious and moral education.
items.correction_markdown: A denominational school follows the national programme and stresses moral and religious values.

items.erreur_markdown: A student answers a question on the importance of school rules with only 'because it is the law'.
items.pourquoi_faux: That gives no explained benefit for pupils.
items.correction_markdown: Say that rules keep order, protect safety, teach responsibility and help learning, and give a short reason for each.

items.erreur_markdown: A student confuses a general school and a technical school and says that a technical school has no teachers.
items.pourquoi_faux: Technical schools have teachers and workshop instructors. They stress practical skills.
items.correction_markdown: Technical schools offer practical training in workshops under teachers and instructors, with tools controlled by the school authorities.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the type of school described in each case: (a) a school opened by a businessman who fixes the fees himself; (b) a school managed by a Catholic mission; (c) a school built and paid for by the State.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Private lay school**, because an individual owns it. (b) **Denominational school**, because a religious body manages it. (c) **Public (government) school**, because the State owns and pays for it.

items.enonce_markdown: State and explain four school rules and the benefit of each for the pupils.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each rule and a mark for each benefit. Possible answers: punctuality, which saves lesson time; wearing the uniform, which creates equality and a sense of belonging; respect for teachers and classmates, which keeps order and good relations; care of school property, which keeps equipment available for everybody; honesty in examinations, which makes certificates credible. Any **four** valid rules with benefits.

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss how pupils can take part in running their school, and say why such participation matters for their future as citizens. [8 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for a balanced answer. Ways: serving as prefects or class monitors; joining clubs and associations; giving opinions through representatives; keeping the compound clean; helping to enforce rules by example; taking part in school projects. Importance: pupils learn responsibility, leadership, teamwork and respect for rules; they practise democracy by choosing and following representatives; and they prepare to take part in community life as adults. **Participation in school is training for citizenship.**

items_markdown: Schools are owned by the State (public), religious bodies (denominational), or individuals or companies (private lay).
Denominational schools stress moral and religious formation but follow the national programme.
Technical schools stress practical skills, and their workshop materials are controlled by the school authorities.
The principal leads the school, teachers teach, prefects assist, and the PTA links parents and school.
The Constitution says that the State guarantees the right to education and organises and supervises it.
School rules protect safety and order and prepare pupils to be responsible citizens.
